subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Caesar Cipher
description: Learn The Caesar Cipher in one minute.

hook.text: Julius Caesar sent military orders using a code so simple a child could crack it today.

buildup.text: He shifted each letter in his messages by three positions. A became D, B became E, and so on.

discovery.text: This substitution cipher kept his messages secret because most people in Rome couldn't read at all.

twist.text: The cipher has only 25 possible shifts. A modern computer cracks it in microseconds.

climax.text: Caesar's cipher was the first widely documented encryption system — simple, elegant, and now obsolete.

punchline.text: Shift three letters. The first encryption was born.

quiz.question: How does the Caesar cipher work?
options: Each letter is shifted by a fixed number of positions in the alphabet
Letters are replaced with random symbols
